data.content:
Plan for knots-4bfa (remove PATH mutation from loom tests):

Root cause: CommandLoomBundleBuilder (src/installed_workflows/loom.rs) resolves
the "loom" binary via std::env::var("KNOTS_LOOM_BIN") falling back to bare
"loom", which Command::spawn resolves through process-global PATH. The two
loom tests in tests_registry_ext.rs mutate PATH via std::env::set_var to
inject a fake "loom" script directory, then restore it. env_lock only
serializes the two loom tests against each other, not against the ~1280
other tests that run in parallel and spawn processes reading the same
process-global PATH, so a losing race can point an unrelated test's
Command::spawn at the wrong PATH.

Fix (matches the knot's preferred injectable-lookup-seam approach; existing
prior art: StubLoomBundleBuilder in src/doctor_fix_tests.rs already proves the
LoomBundleBuilder trait is the intended seam):

1. src/installed_workflows/loom.rs: change CommandLoomBundleBuilder from a
   unit struct to a struct holding an explicit `binary: PathBuf`.
   - `CommandLoomBundleBuilder::new()` preserves today's production
     resolution (KNOTS_LOOM_BIN env var, else "loom" via PATH) -- production
     behavior is unchanged.
   - `#[cfg(test)] CommandLoomBundleBuilder::with_binary(path)` lets a test
     point directly at an absolute script path, bypassing PATH entirely.
   - build_knots_bundle uses `Command::new(&self.binary)` (unchanged spawn
     logic otherwise).
2. src/installed_workflows/operations.rs: update the two production call
   sites (install_bundle, read_bundle_source) to
   `&CommandLoomBundleBuilder::new()`.
3. src/installed_workflows/tests_registry_ext.rs: rewrite
   read_bundle_source_can_shell_out_to_loom and
   loom_failures_and_invalid_utf8_reported to build the fake loom script at
   an absolute path (as today) and call
   `read_bundle_source_with_builder(&package_dir,
   &CommandLoomBundleBuilder::with_binary(&loom_path))` instead of
   mutating PATH and calling read_bundle_source. This keeps real process
   spawning (still proves "can shell out to loom" and the two failure-mode
   assertions), removes both env::set_var("PATH", ...) call sites, and
   drops the now-unneeded env_lock guard from these two tests.
4. src/installed_workflows/tests_helpers.rs: remove env_lock() -- after (3)
   it has no remaining callers in this module tree.
5. src/machine_tests.rs: machine_id_reads_the_process_environment currently
   calls the public machine_id(&root) wrapper, which reads the real
   KNOTS_MACHINE_ID from the ambient process environment, so it fails
   whenever an operator/CI exports KNOTS_MACHINE_ID (a documented override,
   docs/leases.md). Fix using the seam the other tests in this file already
   use (resolve_machine_id takes env_value as a parameter): read
   std::env::var(MACHINE_ID_ENV).ok() once (a read, not a mutation -- safe
   under concurrent tests) and assert machine_id(&root) ==
   resolve_machine_id(that_value, &root). This proves machine_id() is wired
   to the process environment via resolve_machine_id, and is correct
   regardless of whether KNOTS_MACHINE_ID happens to be exported, without
   ever mutating process-global state (other tests across the suite call
   machine_id()/app.machine_id() concurrently, so mutating KNOTS_MACHINE_ID
   even under a lock would reintroduce the same class of flake this knot is
   fixing).

No other std::env::set_var/remove_var call sites touch PATH or
KNOTS_MACHINE_ID; HOME/NO_COLOR/KNO_TRACE/KNOTS_FETCH_BLOB_LIMIT_KB mutations
in other test files are out of this knot's scope (each already uses its own
locally-scoped env_lock and isn't named in the acceptance criteria).

Test strategy:
- Existing tests continue enforcing the same assertions (build success case,
  loom-failure case, invalid-utf8 case, machine-id env-override case) --
  behavior preserved by rewrite, not deletion.
- Verification: cargo test --bin knots run 20x consecutively (clean tree);
  run once more with KNOTS_MACHINE_ID exported; grep for no remaining
  std::env::set_var("PATH", ...) under src/; make sanity.

Risk: low, localized to test-only code plus one small production
constructor-shape change (CommandLoomBundleBuilder gains a private field);
call sites updated in the same commit. No public API surface changes.
